boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Pitzer places for studying, making, moving, gathering, and spending time outdoors.

cards.title: Settle into The Mounds
cards.subtitle: Pellissier Mall, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Bring a book, instrument, or a friend and use the Adirondack chairs or lawn; the college specifically describes this as a place to study and socialize.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped outdoor hub with seating and a fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies The Mounds as a campus activity hub for studying in the sun, socializing, playing music, slacklining, and sitting by the fountain.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; follow current College access policies.

cards.title: Walk the Student Garden
cards.subtitle: Near Mead Hall and Grove House, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Visit the fruit trees, vegetable beds, and chicken coop, or connect with the student garden club if you want to help tend a bed or host an activity.
cards.short_summary: A student-run food garden with a chicken coop.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says the Student Garden is student-run and that its club brings people into the space through events, workshops, art, and other community activities.
cards.access_notes: Pitzer’s campus page states that visitors are welcome 24/7.

cards.title: Take the Outback Preserve slowly
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College campus
cards.notes: Use this conserved landscape for a quiet walk and close observation; treat it as a living-learning site and stay on designated routes where posted.
cards.short_summary: A campus preserve centered on rare alluvial sage scrub.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer describes the Outback Preserve as home to rare Alluvial Sage Scrub and a living-learning laboratory for students, faculty, staff, and the broader community.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor preserve; observe posted conservation and access guidance.

cards.entity_name: Robert Redford Conservancy for Southern California Sustainability
cards.title: Work outdoors at the Redford Conservancy
cards.subtitle: North Campus, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Look for an open-air meeting space or Conservancy program when you need a change from indoor work, then pair the visit with a walk through the conserved land.
cards.short_summary: An environmental learning center beside conserved habitat.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says the Robert Redford Conservancy includes classrooms, creative studios, and open-air meeting spaces on 12 acres of conserved land.
cards.access_notes: The campus map places the Conservancy north of Foothill Boulevard; greenhouse access is by appointment only.

cards.title: Use the Grove House as a change-of-scene desk
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College
cards.notes: Bring work to the bungalow’s study areas or outdoor classroom, and check the campus calendar for readings, open mics, art openings, and music programming.
cards.short_summary: A Craftsman bungalow used for studying, food, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer describes the Grove House as a study space, restaurant, and event venue, and says it hosts open mics, readings, art openings, and Groove at the Grove performances.
cards.access_notes: Some events and restaurant offerings may have their own schedules or requirements.

cards.title: Find a collaborative table at The Nucleus
cards.subtitle: Pitzer–Scripps science facility
cards.notes: Use the collaborative spaces when your project needs a group table or science-adjacent setting; confirm room availability and building access before relying on it.
cards.short_summary: A new science facility with collaborative spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says The Nucleus provides laboratories and collaborative spaces for professors and students across science disciplines and opened in fall 2024.
cards.access_notes: Collaborative and laboratory areas may have access or reservation limits.

cards.title: Move or recharge at Gold Student Center
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College
cards.notes: Plan a wellness break around the gym, pool, or Pilates and yoga studios, and check the College’s current facilities information before you go.
cards.short_summary: Pitzer’s hub for fitness, wellness, and student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says the Gold Student Health & Wellness Center includes yoga and Pilates studios, a gym, pool, Student Senate offices, and a multipurpose programming space.
cards.access_notes: Facility use and class participation may be subject to current campus rules.

cards.title: See what changed on the Free Wall
cards.subtitle: Northeast wall of Mead Hall, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Walk by Mead Hall to see the current iteration, or—if you are a Pitzer student—use the designated wall for public art without the regular committee process.
cards.short_summary: An ever-changing Mead Hall wall for student public art.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies the Free Wall on Mead Hall as the campus location where students may create public art without going through the Aesthetics Committee process.
cards.source_title: The Murals of Pitzer College | Pitzer College
cards.access_notes: The College’s description specifically grants the art-making privilege to students.

cards.title: Meet up by McConnell Center
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College
cards.notes: Use the outdoor area for a casual pickup basketball game or meet before heading to nearby campus destinations; bring your own gear and follow posted court guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named campus center beside an outdoor pickup-game area.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s Student Life page depicts students playing a pickup basketball game outside McConnell Center, and the official campus map lists McConnell Center.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor recreation area; availability may vary with events and campus operations.

cards.title: Make a plant-focused loop through Rodman Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College campus
cards.notes: Use the arboretum as a low-key walking route between campus stops, pausing to notice the drought-tolerant plantings that shape Pitzer’s grounds.
cards.short_summary: A named campus arboretum within Pitzer’s landscaped grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s official campus map lists the Rodman Arboretum, while the College describes its campus landscaping as largely California-native and drought-tolerant.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus grounds; respect landscaping and any posted access guidance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-purchase activities documented by Pitzer and nearby Claremont cultural organizations.

cards.title: Add a piece to the Free Wall
cards.subtitle: Mead Hall, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Bring your own supplies, check the wall’s current layer, and add public art here rather than beginning a separate outdoor-art proposal.
cards.short_summary: A student-designated space for uncensored, changing public art.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies the Free Wall on Mead Hall as the location where students may create public art without the Aesthetics Committee process.
cards.access_notes: Student activity; use the Mead Hall Free Wall and follow campus expectations. The source explicitly says students are free to create art there without committee review.

cards.title: Borrow a Green Bike
cards.subtitle: Green Bike Program, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Ask the student-run shop about a loaner bike, then make a low-key ride around the Claremont Colleges with a friend.
cards.short_summary: A free loaner-bike option for Pitzer students.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says its student-run Green Bike Program lets Pitzer students borrow free loaner bikes from the shop.
cards.access_notes: For Pitzer students; confirm loaner availability with the Green Bike Program before going.

cards.title: Learn a bike fix together
cards.subtitle: Green Bike Program, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Use the shared tools and ask about repair lessons; pick one simple adjustment to practice before heading out on a campus ride.
cards.short_summary: Hands-on bike maintenance with community tools and instruction.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer states that the Green Bike Program gives community members free access to tools and repair lessons.
cards.access_notes: Available to community members according to Pitzer; contact greenbike@students.pitzer.edu for current shop access.

cards.title: Join a Student Garden workshop
cards.subtitle: Pitzer Student Garden, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Check the Garden Club’s current workshop plans, then come ready to learn, make something, or help with a community garden activity.
cards.short_summary: Student Garden programming centered on a shared food-forest space.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer describes the Student Garden as hosting free educational workshops and says no garden experience is necessary to join the Garden Club.
cards.access_notes: Workshop timing varies; contact pzgarden@pitzer.edu or the Garden Club before attending.

cards.title: Volunteer at Pomona Farm
cards.subtitle: Pomona Farm, Pomona College
cards.notes: Coordinate with the Farm before arriving, then spend time tending beds or learning how the campus farm operates with other student volunteers.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost student volunteer experience at Pomona’s working farm.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer states that students can experience Pomona Farm volunteering for free, although non-student volunteers typically need a garden membership.
cards.access_notes: For students; coordinate with Pomona Farm or its volunteer contact in advance.

cards.title: Stop by the chicken coop
cards.subtitle: North side of Mead Hall, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Walk over from Mead Hall, observe the flock quietly, and keep the visit brief so the birds and nearby residents are not disturbed.
cards.short_summary: A casual outdoor stop with Pitzer’s small flock of chickens.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s official walking-tour guide says visitors may stop by the chicken coop on the north side of Mead Hall and greet the flock.
cards.access_notes: Observe from the appropriate public path; do not enter the coop or handle animals. The official tour explicitly invites a stop.

cards.title: See the Claremont Lewis Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 200 W. First Street, Claremont
cards.notes: Bring your student ID, browse the current exhibition at your own pace, and pair the visit with a walk through the adjacent Claremont Village.
cards.short_summary: A Claremont Depot museum with free student admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Lewis Museum of Art lists general admission as free for students.
cards.access_notes: Students are admitted free; check the museum’s current open days and bring student identification if requested.

cards.title: Listen at Fourth Saturdays Poetry
cards.subtitle: Claremont Helen Renwick Library, 208 N. Harvard Ave.
cards.notes: Check the next reader lineup, arrive for the scheduled afternoon start, and stay afterward to discuss a poem or meet other attendees.
cards.short_summary: A recurring public poetry-reading series at the Claremont library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Friends of the Claremont Library describes Fourth Saturdays Poetry Readings as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; confirm the upcoming date because the series schedule can change.

cards.entity_name: Claremont: On the Same Page Community Read
cards.title: Join an On the Same Page event
cards.subtitle: Claremont Helen Renwick Library and local venues
cards.notes: Read as much of the selected book as you like, then choose a related talk or discussion from the community-read event schedule.
cards.short_summary: Free public programs built around Claremont’s annual community read.
cards.evidence_claim: The Friends of the Claremont Library states that all events for its 2025–2026 Claremont Community Read are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; the book may be obtained separately, but attendance at the listed events requires no purchase.

cards.title: Walk Pitzer’s mural-filled campus
cards.subtitle: Begin at Admission Plaza, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Start at Admission Plaza and follow the College’s walking-tour route through Holden Garden, Mead Hall, the Mounds, and the Academic Quad.
cards.short_summary: A self-directed route through named Pitzer campus landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer publishes a walking-tour guide that begins at Admission Plaza and directs visitors through Holden Garden, Mead Hall, the Mounds, and the Academic Quad.
cards.access_notes: The College provides this self-guided campus walking tour; follow campus visitor guidance and avoid residence-only areas.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct study settings in the shared Claremont Colleges Library, a resource identified by Pitzer as serving 7C students.

cards.entity_name: Open Study Area + Government Docs and Microfilm
cards.title: Open Study Area + Government Docs and Microfilm
cards.subtitle: Mudd 1, Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Set up among government documents, maps, microfilm, and print collections; use the nearby microfilm reader when your sources require it.
cards.short_summary: An open study area integrated with government-document and print collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The library identifies Mudd 1 as open study space alongside government documents, maps, microfilm, and print book collections.
cards.access_notes: Enter with a current Claremont Colleges ID card; other visitors must check in at a service desk.

cards.title: Collaborative Commons
cards.subtitle: Honnold 2 North, Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Bring a charged laptop or use the Power Bar, then choose modular seating, pivoting-table chairs, or a media:scape table for collaboration.
cards.short_summary: Flexible open seating with charging and media:scape tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Collaborative Commons is an open study area with modular seating, pivoting-table chairs, media:scape tables, and a Power Bar.
cards.access_notes: Enter with a current Claremont Colleges ID card; other visitors must check in at a service desk.

cards.title: Glass Bridge & Treadmill Desks
cards.subtitle: Between Honnold and Mudd, second floor
cards.notes: Use a treadmill desk when you want a change of posture; the glass bridge connects both library sides and has treetop campus views.
cards.short_summary: Treadmill desks in the library’s glass bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: The library places treadmill desks in the glass bridge between Honnold and Mudd and notes their treetop campus views.
cards.access_notes: Enter with a current Claremont Colleges ID card; other visitors must check in at a service desk.

cards.title: Digital Scholarship Collaboratory
cards.subtitle: Mudd 2 South, Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Choose this open area for projects needing dual monitors, the data-visualization panel, or the listed software suites; bring files ready to work.
cards.short_summary: An open study area with high-performance digital tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Scholarship Collaboratory is an open study area with dual monitors, a data visualization panel, and software suites.
cards.access_notes: Enter with a current Claremont Colleges ID card; other visitors must check in at a service desk.

cards.title: Study Cubes
cards.subtitle: Mudd 2 North & South, Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Use a semi-private cube for solo work or a small group session; the library specifies that these cubes do not require a reservation.
cards.short_summary: Semi-private individual or group-study cubes without reservations.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Cubes in Mudd 2 North and South are semi-private for individual or group study, and reservation is not required.
cards.access_notes: No reservation is required. Enter with a current Claremont Colleges ID card; other visitors must check in.

cards.title: Solarium
cards.subtitle: Mudd 2 East, Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Use the tables and charging ports in natural light, then move to the adjacent outdoor patio when its shaded tables suit your work.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled study space with charging and a shaded patio.
cards.evidence_claim: The Solarium is open study space with natural light, study tables, charging ports, and an outdoor patio with shaded tables.
cards.access_notes: Enter with a current Claremont Colleges ID card; other visitors must check in at a service desk.

cards.title: Mudd 3 Bridge Open Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Mudd 3 Bridge, Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Choose a table or chair on the bridge when you want natural light and treetop views while remaining in an open study area.
cards.short_summary: Open bridge seating with daylight and treetop views.
cards.evidence_claim: Mudd 3 Bridge is an open study area with tables, chairs, natural light, and treetop views.
cards.access_notes: Enter with a current Claremont Colleges ID card; other visitors must check in at a service desk.

cards.title: Honnold & Mudd 3 Open Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Pick from modular desks and tables across the third-floor open areas; use this option when you need flexible seating rather than a room.
cards.short_summary: Third-floor open areas with modular desks and tables.
cards.evidence_claim: The library describes open study areas on Honnold and Mudd 3 as having open seating with modular desks and tables.
cards.access_notes: Enter with a current Claremont Colleges ID card; other visitors must check in at a service desk.

cards.title: Quiet Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Honnold 4 North & South, Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Head to Honnold’s fourth floor for open seating with modular tables when you need an area the library designates for minimal noise distraction.
cards.short_summary: Fourth-floor quiet seating designed to limit distraction.
cards.evidence_claim: Honnold 4 North and South quiet study areas provide open seating, modular tables, and minimal noise distraction.
cards.access_notes: Enter with a current Claremont Colleges ID card; other visitors must check in at a service desk.

cards.title: Study Room 406
cards.subtitle: Honnold 4, Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Reserve this enclosed group-study room when your session benefits from whiteboards and a short-throw projector; collect access details from the library.
cards.short_summary: An enclosed Honnold 4 group-study room with projection.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 406 is an enclosed Honnold 4 group-study room with whiteboards and a short-throw projector.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms are available to current students, faculty, and staff and require a reservation; enter the building with a current ID.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along Claremont Village corridors beside the Claremont Colleges.

cards.title: Folk Music Center
cards.subtitle: 220 N. Yale Ave. — Yale Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk Yale Avenue to browse the Folk Music Center, a named Village music destination listed at 220 N. Yale Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A Yale Avenue stop for a music-focused errand.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Village lists Folk Music Center under Music at 220 N. Yale Ave.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current store access before visiting.

cards.title: Claremont Lewis Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 200 W. First St. — First Street corridor
cards.notes: Head to the Depot on First Street for the Claremont Lewis Museum of Art; the Village lists it among local art galleries.
cards.short_summary: A First Street art stop at the historic depot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Village lists Claremont Lewis Museum of Art as an art gallery at 200 W. First St., Claremont Depot.
cards.access_notes: The Village student-offers page states admission is free for students; check museum visit details before going.

cards.title: Claremont Packing House
cards.subtitle: W. First Street — First Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the Packing House stretch of First Street to combine several named shops, food businesses, studios, and entertainment listings in one stop.
cards.short_summary: A reused-citrus-packing building with clustered destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: The official visitor site identifies the Claremont Packing House as a place to shop and dine in Claremont.
cards.access_notes: Individual tenants set their own access and purchase requirements.

cards.title: Claremont Forum Bookshop & Gallery
cards.subtitle: 544 W. First St. — First Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow First Street to the Packing House for the Claremont Forum Bookshop & Gallery, a named bookshop-and-gallery destination.
cards.short_summary: A First Street stop pairing books with gallery space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Village lists Claremont Forum Bookshop & Gallery at 544 W. First St. in the Packing House.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current access and any event details with the business.

cards.title: Stix Ride Shop
cards.subtitle: 456 W. First St. — First Street corridor
cards.notes: Make First Street your bike-gear corridor by stopping at Stix Ride Shop, listed by the Village at 456 W. First Street.
cards.short_summary: A named First Street destination for ride-related gear.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Village lists Stix Ride Shop at 456 W. First St.
cards.access_notes: Retail purchases may be required for goods or services.

cards.title: Village Dance Arts
cards.subtitle: 111 Harvard Place — Harvard Place corridor
cards.notes: Turn onto Harvard Place for Village Dance Arts, a named local studio and workshop destination listed at 111 Harvard Place.
cards.short_summary: A Harvard Place destination for dance instruction.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Village lists Village Dance Arts under Studios & Workshops at 111 Harvard Place.
cards.access_notes: Contact the studio for current class availability and enrollment requirements.

cards.title: JAX Bicycle Center
cards.subtitle: 217 W. First St. — First Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the First Street corridor for a bike-service or equipment errand at JAX Bicycle Center, listed at 217 W. First Street.
cards.short_summary: A named First Street bike-shop stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Village lists JAX Bicycle Center at 217 W. First St.
cards.access_notes: Retail purchases or service charges may apply.

cards.title: Claremont Chef's Academy
cards.subtitle: 514 W. First St. — First Street corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Packing House on First Street for Claremont Chef's Academy, a named studio-and-workshop listing for culinary classes.
cards.short_summary: A First Street destination for scheduled cooking classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Village lists Claremont Chef's Academy under Studios & Workshops at 514 W. First St. in the Packing House.
cards.access_notes: Classes require advance confirmation and may have fees.

cards.entity_name: Lost Levels Sports Card Shop & TCG
cards.title: Lost Levels Sports Card Shop & TCG
cards.subtitle: 530 W. First St. — First Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop in the Packing House on First Street for Lost Levels, the Village’s named entertainment listing for sports cards and TCGs.
cards.short_summary: A Packing House destination for trading-card interests.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Village lists Lost Levels Sports Card Shop & TCG under Entertainment at 530 W. First St. in the Packing House.
cards.access_notes: Retail purchases may be required for merchandise or events.

cards.title: Some Crust Bakery & Cafe
cards.subtitle: 119 Yale Ave. — Yale Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use Yale Avenue for a bakery-and-café stop at Some Crust, which the Village lists at 119 Yale Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A named Yale Avenue bakery and café destination.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Village lists Some Crust Bakery & Cafe at 119 Yale Ave. under Dining.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; confirm current service details with the café.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Pitzer rituals and recurring campus practices, from a comet-named festival to an ever-changing student art wall.

cards.title: Follow the comet to Kohoutek
cards.subtitle: Annual Pitzer music and arts festival
cards.notes: Look for the annual festival schedule and experience the event that Pitzer identifies as its first and oldest tradition, named for the 1973 comet.
cards.short_summary: A comet-inspired music and arts festival with roots in the 1970s.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer calls Kohoutek its annual music and arts festival, first and oldest tradition, and says it is named after a comet that appeared in 1973.
cards.access_notes: Check Pitzer’s event communications for the current festival date, location, and attendance details.

cards.title: See Rockabilly’s annual return
cards.subtitle: Latinx Student Union festival
cards.notes: Watch for the Latinx Student Union’s yearly festival, which centers SoCal Latinx art, music, and car culture while supporting community organizations.
cards.short_summary: An annual Latinx arts, music, and car-culture festival.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer states that its Latinx Student Union sponsors Rockabilly each year; since 2007 it has celebrated SoCal Latinx art, music, and car culture.
cards.access_notes: Pitzer says the festival is open to all students; consult current organizers for event details.

cards.title: Mark Tuesday night with Snackie Snack
cards.subtitle: Tuesday 9 p.m. community treat
cards.notes: Plan around the weekly Tuesday 9 p.m. gathering described by Pitzer, then confirm the current location and offering through campus communications.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Tuesday-night treat and community gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s 2025–26 viewbook describes Snackie Snack as a special treat and community-sharing occasion at 9 p.m. on Tuesdays.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies Tuesday at 9 p.m.; confirm whether it is occurring during the current academic term.

cards.title: Start spring at Pitzer Palooza
cards.subtitle: Spring-semester kickoff festival
cards.notes: Watch the campus calendar as spring begins for Pitzer Palooza, the festival Pitzer identifies as a kickoff to the spring semester.
cards.short_summary: A festival associated with opening the spring semester.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s 2025–26 viewbook lists Pitzer Palooza among its music and art festivals and describes it as kicking off spring semester.
cards.access_notes: Check current campus programming for date, location, and participation information.

cards.title: Catch Citrus Fest at the Grove House
cards.subtitle: Grove House and Student Garden festival
cards.notes: Look for Citrus Fest programming at the Grove House and Student Garden, and use the current event listing to confirm activities and access.
cards.short_summary: A themed festival tied to Pitzer’s Grove House and Student Garden.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s 2025–26 viewbook names Citrus Fest as a themed festival at the Grove House and Student Garden.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current year’s schedule and participation details with Pitzer before attending.

cards.title: Look for Harvest Fest
cards.subtitle: Grove House and Student Garden festival
cards.notes: Check seasonal campus programming for Harvest Fest at the Grove House and Student Garden, then follow the listed guidance for participating.
cards.short_summary: A harvest-themed gathering connected to Pitzer’s garden spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s 2025–26 viewbook identifies Harvest Fest as a themed festival at the Grove House and Student Garden.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current year’s schedule and participation details with Pitzer before attending.

cards.title: Listen in at Storyteller’s Festival
cards.subtitle: Community Engagement Center and Writing Center festival
cards.notes: Watch for this themed festival and consult the organizing centers’ announcements for its current format, speakers, location, and attendance guidance.
cards.short_summary: A recurring storytelling-centered festival supported by campus centers.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s 2025–26 viewbook lists Storyteller’s Festival among its themed festivals and credits the Community Engagement Center and Writing Center.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current event details with Pitzer’s Community Engagement Center or Writing Center.

cards.title: Read the Free Wall, then add your voice
cards.subtitle: Mead Hall’s changing public-art wall
cards.notes: Visit the north-east wall of Mead Hall to see the latest student expression; students may create public art there without the usual committee process.
cards.short_summary: A designated Mead Hall wall that changes with student expression.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies the Free Wall on Mead Hall as the campus location where students may create public art without going through the Aesthetics Committee process.
cards.source_title: The Murals of Pitzer College | Pitzer College
cards.access_notes: Located on a north-east wall of Mead Hall; follow campus public-art guidance and posted instructions.

cards.title: Take the mic at Shakedown Sounds
cards.subtitle: Bi-weekly Shakedown Café open mic
cards.notes: Check the current campus events calendar for a Shakedown Sounds date, then attend or participate in the bi-weekly open-mic format at Shakedown Café.
cards.short_summary: A bi-weekly open mic hosted at the campus café.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer describes Shakedown Sounds as a bi-weekly open mic at the Shakedown Café.
cards.access_notes: Pitzer describes the event as bi-weekly; verify the current date, time, and participation details before going.

cards.title: Begin with an Orientation Adventure
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation off-campus trips
cards.notes: Incoming students choose an off-campus small-group trip before classes, with options updated each summer; complete the orientation registration when it opens.
cards.short_summary: Pitzer’s recurring off-campus introduction for new students.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer describes Orientation Adventures as the off-campus component of New Student Orientation, designed to build relationships while students explore Southern California.
cards.access_notes: For new students; Pitzer says trip options and details are updated each summer before fall orientation.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Pitzer College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, on-campus first-weekend sequence: get oriented, eat, explore Pitzer’s outdoor spaces, make something, and finish with art.

cards.title: Start at Avery Gate
cards.subtitle: Arrival point on the Pitzer campus map
cards.notes: Use this named campus landmark as a starting point, then pull up the interactive map before walking toward the central academic area.
cards.short_summary: Begin by getting your bearings at a named campus entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s current campus map identifies Avery Gate as location 32.
cards.access_notes: Use the college’s interactive campus map for wayfinding.

cards.title: Settle in on The Mounds
cards.subtitle: Pellissier Mall, Pitzer campus
cards.notes: Bring a book, sketchpad, or new hallmate for a daytime pause on this central lawn before continuing across campus.
cards.short_summary: Take a relaxed outdoor break in Pitzer’s central green space.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s walking tour describes The Mounds as a grass section running from Brant Clock Tower to McConnell Center and a site for orientation and campus events.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; check the campus calendar if an event is scheduled.

cards.title: Have a meal at McConnell Bistro
cards.subtitle: McConnell Center dining hall
cards.notes: Check the day’s menu, then use a meal-plan option or another eligible payment method for a first shared campus meal.
cards.short_summary: Eat together at Pitzer’s seven-day dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer states that McConnell Bistro serves made-from-scratch meals seven days a week and offers several food stations.
cards.access_notes: Dining requires an applicable meal plan or payment; consult the current menu for service details.

cards.title: Pick up something at Shakedown Café
cards.subtitle: Pitzer campus café
cards.notes: Make this a casual stop for a snack or drink, and check the café’s current serving information before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Add a café stop centered on seasonal, locally sourced food.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says the student-started Shakedown Café focuses on sustainable, seasonal, and locally sourced goods.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase or applicable dining funds; verify current offerings before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Mead Hall murals
cards.subtitle: Mead Hall exterior and hallways
cards.notes: Take a slow lap to look at the student-made murals, then photograph only what is appropriate in an active residence hall.
cards.short_summary: See a long-running, student-created layer of Pitzer’s campus art.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer describes Mead Hall as historically known for student murals on its exterior walls and hallways spanning decades.
cards.access_notes: Mead Hall is a residence hall; respect residents and posted access guidance.

cards.title: Check what’s happening at Grove House
cards.subtitle: Performance and meeting space on campus
cards.notes: Look for an open mic, reading, art opening, or Groove at the Grove listing, then attend only the event’s posted public or student access.
cards.short_summary: Use a named arts venue to find a low-pressure community event.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says Grove House hosts open mics, readings, art openings, and Groove at the Grove music performances.
cards.access_notes: Programming varies; confirm event time and eligibility on Pitzer’s calendar.

cards.title: Take the Outback trail
cards.subtitle: Northeast Pitzer campus, north of East and West Halls
cards.notes: Enter from north of East and West Halls, stay on the trail, and pack out anything you bring to help protect the restoration area.
cards.short_summary: Walk through Pitzer’s rare alluvial sage scrub preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies the Outback Preserve as over three acres of alluvial sage scrub and directs visitors to stay on the trail.
cards.access_notes: Stay on designated trails; follow the preserve’s no-smoking and pack-out guidance.

cards.entity_name: Gold Student Health and Wellness Center
cards.title: Move at the Gold Student Center
cards.subtitle: GSC, near Pitzer’s first-year residence halls
cards.notes: Use the gym, pool, or Pilates and yoga studios according to the facility’s current student access rules and class schedule.
cards.short_summary: Build in a recreation stop close to the first-year halls.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies the Gold Student Health and Wellness Center as an on-campus recreation home with a gym, pool, and Pilates and yoga studios.
cards.access_notes: Facility and class access are subject to current student policies and schedules.

cards.title: See what’s on at Nichols Gallery
cards.subtitle: Broad Center, 1060 N. Mills Ave.
cards.notes: Visit during the posted Wednesday–Saturday afternoon hours, or contact the gallery in advance if you need to arrange another time.
cards.short_summary: End with a free contemporary-art stop in the Broad Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer states that Nichols Gallery is in the Broad Center, exhibitions are always free, and regular hours are Wednesday–Saturday, 1–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours: Wednesday–Saturday, 1–4 p.m.; exhibitions may be viewed outside those hours by appointment.

cards.title: Continue to Lenzner Gallery
cards.subtitle: Atherton Hall, 1150 Pitzer Service Rd.
cards.notes: Pair this gallery with Nichols if both are open, and use the accessible path or drop-off information if that makes the visit easier.
cards.short_summary: Complete the art walk at Pitzer’s second free exhibition space.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer lists the Lenzner Family Art Gallery in Atherton Hall and says its exhibitions are always free.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours: Wednesday–Saturday, 1–4 p.m.; both galleries are wheelchair accessible.
